correctness.rationale: The focal Martínez-Fernández–Tradacete paper was read in arXiv HTML. Proposition 3.14 gives the unit ball as the closed solid convex hull of canonical factor balls; approximate each z_j by a vector dominated by sum_i φ_i(a_ij) with sum_i||a_ij|| <=||z_j||. Lattice supremum is bounded by sum_i φ_i(sup_j a_ij); Proposition 3.10 identifies the norm of this positive linear sum with the ℓ1 sum of factor norms. Applying upper-p estimates, Hölder in factor index, and ℓp<=ℓ1 for nonnegative grouped masses gives r^(1-1/p). Approximation-to-limit follows Lipschitz continuity of finite lattice suprema. For scalar factors, Proposition 3.13 gives the exact norm on the positive ℓinfinity sphere; max_i u_i=1 has norm r while each coordinate generator has norm 1, attaining the factor. Boundary r=1 gives constant 1.
residual_risks: The result is finite r and real Banach lattices, 1<p<infinity, normalized per-factor constants <=1. No unequal-constant exact formula is claimed.

evidence: The focal full HTML preprint explicitly proves qualitative upper-p stability for two factors in Proposition 8.5, while its sharp 2^(1-1/p) formula is for the strictly stronger p-convexity hypothesis (Proposition 8.3 and Remark 8.4). It does not state the universal finite-factor quantitative upper-p constant. The new proof uses its construction rather than reclaiming it.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A p-convexity theorem bounds (sum|z_j|^p)^(1/p) and does not imply every free product is p-convex when merely given upper-p factors. Prop 8.5 is qualitative for two factors; no coefficient and no all-r sharpness. Free Banach lattices with upper-p estimates generated by a Banach space are categorically distinct from the ordinary lattice free product here.

value.rationale: Quantitative stability with the best finite-factor cost answers the natural next invariant after the primary paper establishes categorical existence and qualitative upper-p stability. The scalar free product yields an exact universal extremal family, so the coefficient is neither arbitrary nor a tiny unmotivated gain.
residual_risks: The Hölder step is elementary once the primary ball representation is known; its value is the exact sharp global transfer theorem rather than the inequality step alone.

final_claim: For finite free products of r real Banach lattices with upper p-estimate constants <=1 (1<p<infinity), the optimal universal upper p constant is r^(1-1/p), attained for r scalar factors.
